recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Changes to the historical operationdefinition-profile extension should be made in the FHIR Extension Pack if needed; any further core redesign of OperationDefinition parameter profile/targetProfile naming would require a new work-group decision.
issue_request: FHIR-17725 was Published/Not Persuasive with Modification for STU3. It asked for a way to specify the profile that applies when an operation parameter value is a directly embedded resource, not only when the parameter is a canonical or Reference target; the approved resolution was an OperationDefinition.parameter profile extension legal on all parameter types, with possible R5 elevation to core.
initial_application: Git commit b7251b1f8b23b2fe0f46e6b5fc977cbf36ac6ec3 applied the issue by adding operationdefinition.parameter.profile support to the OperationDefinition spreadsheet. Current source/fhir.ini also preserves an old-to-new mapping from OperationDefinition.parameter.profile to OperationDefinition.parameter.targetProfile.
additional_context: OperationDefinition is active in the current build. The legacy operationdefinition-profile StructureDefinition is now maintained in the FHIR Extension Pack, not in this core checkout. Later Published issue FHIR-26411 elevated the inline-resource targetProfile behavior into core for R5 and is already represented on the combined branch; later same-family reconciliations for FHIR-39345 and FHIR-44690 are also already represented and explain the current opd-3/all-resource-types rule and clarified targetProfile prose.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current build-scoped OperationDefinition StructureDefinition already allows targetProfile for Reference, canonical, and resource parameter types and explicitly describes profile/IG constraints applying to the inline resource instance. No core source edit is needed for this seed.
